screening_decisions.reason: Focuses on compliance but does not clearly measure clinical outcomes like BMD or fracture rates
RCT testing adherence therapy for schizophrenia; measures both medication adherence (secondary outcome) and clinical outcomes (PANSS scores); 8-week follow-up
RCT of pharmacist adherence counseling for H. pylori treatment; measures self-reported adherence and clinical outcome (eradication rate); 90.7% follow-up at 3 months
Intervention targets physician prescribing behavior, not patient medication adherence
RCT testing free glucometer strips to increase monitoring; measures SBGM frequency (adherence) and HbA1c (clinical outcome); 12-month follow-up
RCT of education and telephone case management for pediatric diabetes; measures adherence (ADH scores) and HbA1c; 6-month follow-up
RCT of nurse-delivered CAP-IT adherence intervention for HIV; measures 5 adherence measures and clinical outcomes (CD4, viral load); 6-month follow-up
Family intervention mentions adherence in background but unclear if measured as primary outcome
RCT of pharmaceutical care for Type 2 diabetes; measures medication adherence and clinical outcomes (HbA1c, BP, Framingham risk); 97.5% follow-up at 12 months
RCT of lottery-based incentives for warfarin adherence; measures adherence and clinical outcome (INR levels); 6-month follow-up
Compares dosing schedules, not an adherence intervention
RCT of medication compliance feedback and monitoring; measures adherence (MEMS) and clinical outcomes (drinking outcomes); 52-week follow-up
Compares ulcer prevention drugs, not an adherence intervention
Focuses on BP control and medication changes, adherence not clearly measured as outcome
Compares antibiotics, not an adherence intervention
RCT of asthma care training for children; measures self-reported compliance behaviors and clinical outcomes (ER visits, hospitalization); 12-month follow-up
RCT of intensive medication counselling for heart failure; measures adherence (tablet count) and clinical outcomes (exercise test, breathlessness, edema); 3-month follow-up
Focuses on adherence measurement, unclear if clinical outcomes measured
RCT of DOT-ART for HIV; measures adherence (viral load as proxy) and clinical outcomes (CD4 count, survival); 12-24 month follow-up
RCT of telephone intervention for heart failure; measures compliance indicators and clinical outcomes (death, hospitalization); 1-3 year follow-up
RCT of health education for overactive bladder; measures medication compliance/persistence and clinical outcomes (symptom severity); 16-week follow-up
RCT of multiple-family psychoeducation for schizophrenia; measures medication compliance and clinical outcomes (relapse, rehospitalization); 2-year follow-up
Observational/correlational study, not an RCT
RCT of pharmacist home follow-up for elderly; measures compliance and clinical outcomes (readmission rates); 90-day follow-up
Spiritual assessment not primarily an adherence intervention

RCT of CBT-AD intervention to improve medication adherence in HIV patients. Measures adherence (MEMs) and clinical outcomes (depression, HIV RNA). Follow-up includes 6 and 12 months. Meets all criteria.
RCT of health education for asthma adherence. Measures adherence but no clear clinical outcome (lung function, exacerbations) is reported. Only adherence improvement percentages are given.
RCT of medication monitors for TB compliance. Measures adherence/compliance but no clinical outcome (cure rates, treatment success) is reported. Focuses only on default rates.

RCT of lay health mentoring for ischaemic heart disease. While medication usage is mentioned as an outcome, the intervention focuses on diet and physical activity, not specifically medication adherence. No significant medication adherence results reported.

RCT of family-focused therapy for bipolar disorder. Measures adherence and clinical outcomes (relapse, mood symptoms). However, follow-up rates are below 80% (FFT 71%, CM 61%), failing the selection criteria.

RCT of psychoeducational programme for schizophrenia patients and relatives. Measures compliance/adherence and clinical outcomes (relapse, psychopathology). 1-year follow-up. Meets criteria despite null findings on compliance.
RCT of personalized risk communication. While adherence is measured, the intervention is not designed to improve adherence but rather to communicate risk. No impact on adherence was found.
Cluster-RCT of shared decision making intervention to improve antipsychotic compliance. Measures long-term compliance and rehospitalizations. 6-month and 18-month follow-up. Meets criteria.
RCT comparing group vs individual diabetes education. Does not measure medication adherence as an outcome. Focuses on HbA1c, knowledge, self-management behaviors.
Randomized registry study of reminders for pravastatin compliance. Measures adherence but no clinical outcome (cardiovascular events, mortality) is reported. Only lifestyle modifications assessed.
Observational analysis within DPP RCT examining adherence predictors. Not an intervention study to improve adherence - rather analyzes adherence patterns within an existing trial.
RCT of family-based vs individual therapy for schizophrenia. Does not measure medication adherence as an outcome. Focuses on exacerbations, hospital admissions, psychopathology.
RCT of health education strategies for TB chemoprophylaxis compliance. Measures adherence but no clinical outcome (TB development, infection rates) is reported.
RCT of pharmacy-based coaching program for antidepressant adherence. Measures adherence (electronic pill container) and clinical outcomes (depressive symptoms). Meets criteria.

RCT of depression relapse prevention program targeting medication adherence. Measures adherence to long-term pharmacotherapy and clinical outcomes (depression relapse, symptoms). 12-month follow-up. Meets criteria.
Meta-analysis of observational studies, not an RCT. Does not meet study design criteria.
Open-label extension study comparing two medications, not an adherence intervention. Measures adherence but intervention is not designed to improve adherence.
RCT of internet-based self-management for asthma. Does not measure medication adherence as an outcome. Focuses on quality of life, asthma control, lung function, exacerbations.
RCT of telephone counselling by pharmacist to improve compliance in polypharmacy patients. Measures compliance score and clinical outcome (mortality). 2-year follow-up. Meets criteria.
Describes development and implementation of IVR system but does not report RCT results with adherence and clinical outcomes. Appears to be a descriptive article.
RCT of cognitive therapy for bipolar disorder. While adherence is measured, the intervention is not designed to improve adherence but to treat bipolar disorder. Adherence is a secondary outcome.
RCT of self-management counseling for heart failure. Does not measure medication adherence as an outcome. Primary endpoint is death or hospitalization, secondary endpoints do not include adherence.

Pilot RCT of integrated care intervention for depression and hypertension. Measures adherence (MEMS) to both antidepressant and antihypertensive medications and clinical outcomes (depression scores, blood pressure). 6-week follow-up. Meets criteria.
RCT of automated telephone monitoring and counseling for hypertension. Measures medication adherence and clinical outcome (blood pressure). 6-month follow-up. Meets criteria.

RCT comparing tablet vs syrup formulations for malaria treatment adherence. Measures adherence but no clinical outcome (fever resolution, parasite clearance) is reported. Only adherence and cost assessed.
RCT with adherence intervention and clinical outcomes, but only 275/532 (52%) patients remained throughout the study, which is below the required 80% follow-up threshold.

This study compares dosing regimens of the same drug rather than testing an intervention designed to improve adherence. The intervention is the drug formulation/schedule itself, not an adherence-enhancing strategy.

Compares different formulations/dosing schedules of metoprolol rather than testing an active intervention to improve adherence. Simplification of regimen is inherent to the drug choice, not an adherence intervention.

While this is an RCT with clinical outcomes, the intervention focuses on increasing visit frequency and case management rather than directly improving medication adherence. Medication adherence is not measured as an outcome.
This is an observational/cross-sectional study exploring predictors of adherence using the health belief model. It is not an RCT testing an intervention to improve adherence.

RCT testing monitoring and feedback intervention with adherence measured, but no clinical outcomes are reported. The study only reports compliance measures (self-report, lithium levels, appointment-keeping, refill frequency).

Phase 2 is a 12-month RCT with nurse-led intervention targeting non-adherence. Both adherence (improved from 37.6% to 61.9%) and clinical outcomes (reduced oral steroids, hospital admissions) are measured.

Compares dosing frequencies of different drugs rather than testing an intervention to improve adherence. The study examines compliance patterns as an outcome of drug choice, not an adherence intervention.
12-month RCT with telemonitoring intervention. Reports improved compliance with therapy along with clinical outcomes (mortality, hospitalizations, cholesterol levels).

Preliminary investigation with unclear RCT design. No significant differences found in health practices at 6-month follow-up. Does not clearly demonstrate an effective adherence intervention with clinical outcomes.
RCT comparing combined treatment vs medication alone for depression. The intervention is psychotherapy added to medication, not an adherence intervention. Medication adherence is not measured.
28-month RCT with collaborative care intervention. Reports improved antidepressant adherence (measured at 6 and 12 months) and clinical outcomes (depressive symptoms).

6-month RCT with health coaching intervention including counseling on medication adherence. Reports improved blood pressure control. Adherence counseling is part of the intervention, though adherence itself may not be directly measured.
RCT testing incentives and DOT for LTBI treatment. Measures adherence (percentage taken, completion rates) but does not report clinical outcomes such as treatment success or disease progression.
Abstract is too brief to determine study design, intervention details, or outcomes. Insufficient information to assess eligibility.
RCT comparing ED dispensing vs pharmacy pickup. While pharmacy fill rates differed, actual medication-taking was unknown. No difference in clinical outcomes (return visits, admissions).
RCT comparing DOT vs self-administration during TB hospitalization. Measures treatment completion/default rates but does not report clinical outcomes such as sputum conversion or cure rates.
2-year RCT but intervention focuses on self-treatment guidelines for asthma management, not medication adherence. Adherence is not measured as an outcome.
RCT testing written information intervention with adherence measured (pill counts), but no clinical outcomes are reported. Only compliance rates are presented.
1-year RCT with family-focused intervention and clinical outcomes (A1c), but medication adherence is not measured. Intervention focuses on family involvement in diabetes tasks.
Factorial RCT comparing drugs and education levels. Primary focus is on INR stability, not adherence improvement. Education intervention showed no difference in outcomes.
5-week RCT testing behavioral strategies for peak flow monitoring adherence, not medication adherence. Short follow-up period and different adherence target.
18-month RCT with nurse-led counseling intervention. Reports significantly higher statin adherence and improved clinical outcomes (lower LDL cholesterol).
11-week RCT with adherence therapy intervention. Reports improved adherence (37% increase) and clinical outcomes (significant BP reduction).
Study design unclear from abstract - appears to be a before-after study comparing to national data rather than an RCT. No control group mentioned.

While this RCT measures both compliance and clinical outcomes (HbA1c), the intervention is stress management training aimed at improving glucose metabolism, not specifically designed to improve medication adherence. The intervention does not target adherence behaviors.

RCT testing telephonic intervention to improve diabetes control. Measures medication adherence (pharmacy claims data, self-report) and clinical outcomes (A1C). 1-year follow-up. Meets all selection criteria.

This is Part A of a study focusing on process description and pharmacist satisfaction, not clinical outcomes or adherence measurements. Main outcomes are number of modules provided and medication changes suggested, not adherence or clinical outcomes.

RCT testing simple arrangements to improve compliance in hypertensives. Measures compliance (dropout rates) and clinical outcomes (blood pressure lowering). 1-year follow-up. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT comparing two dosing schedules of the same antibiotic, not an intervention to improve adherence. While compliance was mentioned as similar between groups, it was not measured as an outcome. Short 7-day treatment course.

RCT testing bone marker feedback intervention to improve adherence to ibandronate. Measures adherence at 6 and 12 months. Clinical outcomes include serum CTX levels. 12-month follow-up. Meets selection criteria.

RCT testing compliance therapy to improve adherence in schizophrenia. Measures compliance with drug treatment at one year and clinical outcomes (symptomatology, quality of life, rehospitalization). Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing dosing intervals of the same antibiotic, not an intervention to improve adherence. Adherence was not measured as an outcome. Short 14-day treatment course for acute infection.
RCT testing pharmacist intervention to improve diabetes management and adherence. Measures self-reported adherence and clinical outcomes (HbA1c). 12-month follow-up. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT testing patient education intervention, but does not measure medication adherence as an outcome. Only measures HRQoL and FEV1. Does not meet the requirement to measure both adherence and clinical outcomes.

RCT comparing dosing frequencies of topical antifungal, not an intervention to improve adherence. While OD administration 'improves compliance' is mentioned, adherence was not measured as an outcome. Short 4-week treatment.

RCT testing multiple compliance-improving strategies (counselling, special container, self-recording, reminders). Measures compliance (plasma levels, prescription refills) and clinical outcomes (seizure frequency). 6-month follow-up. Meets all selection criteria.

This RCT compares treatment duration (3 vs 5 days of amoxicillin) rather than testing an adherence intervention. While non-adherence is mentioned as a risk factor for treatment failure, the study does not evaluate an intervention designed to improve medication adherence.

RCT testing pharmacy discharge plan intervention. Measures adherence to prescribed medication (secondary outcome) and clinical outcomes (re-admission, mortality, etc.). Follow-up is 6 months. Hospital data collected on 91% of patients meets the 80% follow-up criterion. Conservative inclusion due to borderline follow-up rates.

While this is a controlled intervention study with psychoeducational training, the abstract states 'the groups did not differ' regarding medication management. The study reports attitude changes but no clear clinical outcomes related to medication adherence improvement.

RCT with family-based intervention including medication management component. However, the abstract explicitly states differences 'were not explained by differences in drug compliance', indicating adherence was not measured as an outcome. Only clinical outcomes (rehospitalization, employment) are reported.

Clinical trial testing motivational interviewing for ART adherence. Adherence measured by MEMS. However, no clinical outcomes (e.g., viral load, CD4 count) are mentioned in the abstract. Only risk reduction behaviors are reported as secondary outcomes.

RCT testing nurse-delivered adherence intervention for ART. Measures both adherence (self-report and EDM) and clinical outcomes (HIV-1 RNA viral load, CD4 count). Follow-up is 25 weeks (~6 months). Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing treatment modalities (sertraline, IPT, combination) for dysthymia. This is a treatment effectiveness study, not an adherence intervention study. Adherence is not measured as an outcome.

RCT testing patient-operated hypertension group intervention for previously noncompliant patients. Measures adherence (pill counts) and clinical outcomes (blood pressure). Follow-up extends to 6 months. Meets all selection criteria.

Cluster-RCT comparing two interventions to improve depression treatment. Explicitly measures adherence to antidepressant medication and depression outcomes. Follow-up is 26 weeks (~6 months). Meets all selection criteria.
RCT testing programmable medication reminder device (DMAS) for HIV patients. Measures adherence and clinical outcomes (quality of life scales). Follow-up is 6 months. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT testing SMS reminders for ART adherence. Adherence measured by MEMS. However, no clinical outcomes (e.g., viral load, CD4 count) are mentioned in the abstract. Only adherence and treatment interruption outcomes are reported.

RCT comparing asthma clinics to standard care. While medication use is measured, this is not specifically an adherence intervention study. The intervention focuses on overall asthma management (counseling, education, spirometry) rather than specifically improving medication adherence.

Double-blind RCT comparing two antidepressants. While adherence is measured via MEMS, this is a treatment comparison study, not an adherence intervention. Additionally, follow-up is only 9 weeks, which is less than 6 months required for long-term treatments.

RCT testing education intervention for asthma/COPD patients on medication. Measures compliance (adherence) and clinical outcomes (symptoms, quality of life). Follow-up 1-2 years exceeds 6-month requirement. Intervention targets technical skills and coping which relate to medication adherence.

Multicentre RCT with telephone intervention including education, counselling, and monitoring to enhance drug therapy compliance. Measures clinical outcomes (mortality, hospital admission). 99.5% follow-up exceeds 80% requirement. Intervention explicitly targets medication adherence.

RCT with family intervention including education about illness and methods of dealing with patient. Explicitly measures regular medication use and shows independent/additive effects with medication adherence. Clinical outcomes include hospital readmission and functioning. 18-month follow-up adequate.

RCT but intervention targets fluid intake behavior, not prescribed medication adherence. While it measures clinical outcomes (dehydration markers), the intervention does not address medication adherence as required by selection criteria.

RCT comparing dosing regimens with adherence measurement. However, follow-up is only 12 weeks, which is less than the 6-month minimum required for long-term treatments. Does not meet follow-up duration criterion.

RCT testing supportive measures (reminder stickers, timers, physician-patient interaction) to improve drug adherence. Uses electronic monitoring for adherence assessment. Measures BP control as clinical outcome. 34-week follow-up exceeds 6-month requirement.

RCT specifically targeting treatment adherence in psychotic disorders using compliance therapy based on motivational interviewing. Measures observer-rated compliance and clinical outcomes (social functioning, community tenure, readmission). 18-month follow-up adequate.

RCT testing pharmaceutical care intervention. Explicitly measures medication adherence and BP as clinical outcome. 12-month follow-up exceeds requirements. Intervention targets medication compliance enhancement.

RCT with telephone-based education and monitoring by pharmacists targeting antidepressant adherence. Measures adherence at 3 and 6 months and depression symptoms as clinical outcome. 6-month follow-up meets minimum requirement.

RCT comparing two medications for OCD efficacy, not an adherence intervention. While it mentions compliance benefits, adherence is not measured as an outcome. This is a drug comparison trial, not an adherence intervention study.

RCT with nurse case management including pharmacologic intervention and lifestyle modification. Measures being on lipid-lowering medication (persistence/adherence proxy) and LDL-C levels as clinical outcome. 1-year follow-up adequate. Intervention supports medication management.
This is a systematic review methodology paper, not an RCT. It describes methods for conducting a review of decision support systems. Does not meet the RCT requirement.

RCT testing sunscreen efficacy, not an adherence intervention. While it measures adherence with cream use, the primary purpose is evaluating sunscreen effectiveness, not improving medication adherence. Adherence is examined as a confounding factor, not as an intervention target.
This is a study design/preliminary report for the DIAL trial (same as study 502). Does not present complete results. Likely duplicate/overlap with study 502 which contains the full trial results.

RCT testing educational videotape intervention targeting treatment behavior/adherence (test-of-cure return rate). Measures adherence-related outcomes and knowledge. Conservative inclusion as intervention targets treatment completion behavior.

RCT with pharmacist protocol including drug adherence support. Measures statin adherence rates and cardiovascular risk factors as clinical outcomes. Minimum 6-month follow-up meets requirement. Intervention explicitly includes adherence support.

Cluster RCT with peer health workers providing adherence support for ART. Measures adherence (pill count) and virologic failure as clinical outcome. Follow-up up to 192 weeks exceeds requirements. Intervention explicitly targets ART adherence.

RCT with self-management program including adherence-enhancing strategies. Measures adherence and functional status/hospital visits as clinical outcomes. 1-year follow-up adequate. Intervention explicitly targets adherence improvement.
